summary: Set 112 Session 2 of 3: the extension surface and the teaching docs lose the Lightweight tier, after Session 1 removed the router. The Getting Started form's tier fork is GONE -- its first question is now provider access (direct DABBLER_* keys vs a Copilot CLI seat), the only setup fork the one-tier workflow still has. Seven extension modules deleted whole (switchTier, setupVerification, externalVerification, tierRewrite, verificationModeRewrite, tierMarkerStore, tierLegibility) plus eight test modules and the 26-file uat-matrix/hello-world-lightweight fixture tree; tierLegibility's one tier-independent export -- the Set 086 verdict vocabulary -- moved to utils/verdictTokens.ts rather than dying with its host. Four row actions left package.json and ActionRegistry. types.ts lost five types and eight fields; the scan layer stopped deriving six SessionSet fields only the Lightweight Explorer signals read; the webview lost the tier radio, the verification-mode block, and their gsState/seed machinery. Templates render one tier and the cold-start/full golden was regenerated from them (never hand-edited). Docs: the workflow doc lost its 383-line Lightweight verification section AND the typed-session procedure whose writers S1 deleted (S1 flagged that as a live trap); the constitution, spec-md-schema, session-state-schema, authoring guide, quick-start, README and the extension README tell one story; tier-model.md is a historical note explaining what went and why; the stale-framing drift guard retired with the tier it defended, keeping its doc-walk mechanism (commented) for S3's grep gate. docs/cross-repo-lightweight-removal-notice.md is authored and ready -- SENDING IT IS OPERATOR-GATED. TWO DEFECTS FOUND RATHER THAN INHERITED. (1) The shipped sample project would have broken for every user of 'Dabbler: Try a sample project': its spec declared tier: lightweight, which S1's loader now refuses, and its honest verification_method: 'skipped' close lost its sanctioned home the moment --no-router stopped relieving gates. It now ships ai_router/budget.yaml with threshold_usd: 0 and a matching method -- the operator-declared exception check_verification_integrity names -- proven by the smoke test's real close_session run. (2) The three Evaluate prompts and their instruction doc still ordered a reviewing engine to write external-verification.md 'or it does not count', citing a close gate whose parser S1 deleted; reframed as advisory (journaled). Cross-provider verification (gpt-5.5; orchestrator provider anthropic excluded) returned two Major findings on a 2-lens discovery fan-out, both naming one real miss: the collapse never reached the extension's Marketplace README, which still sold two tiers and named four deleted commands. Accepted and fixed, along with twelve 'Full tier' qualifiers across nine live docs that now imply a second tier exists. Supplementary pass found nothing new; remediation-review returned VERIFIED, 1 fix accepted 0 rejected. Runs of record after the last change: pytest 3,561 passed / 9 skipped; mocha 1,602 passing; Playwright 33 passed -- including a rewritten Layer 3 test that asserts the tier fork's ABSENCE with stale .dabbler markers on disk (they must be inert) and the real first-run walkthrough driving an actual Build through the form. Three system-status Layer 3 tests stopped depending on the tier to suppress the provider-key fault and seed a dummy key explicitly instead. drift_guard and tutorial_gate exit 0. THIRD DEFECT, found by this session's own close-out: close_session died with a raw TRACEBACK instead of a gate refusal. The close backstop calls assemble_evidence, which raises EvidenceTooLargeError -- deliberately not a VerifySessionError, because the CLI maps it to its own exit code -- and the backstop caught only VerifySessionError. Any session whose diff overruns the evidence cap (a property of removal sets like this one) hit it, at exactly the moment an operator most needs to be told what to do. Fixed: the backstop now returns verification_unavailable naming the Step 6 command and its --exclude / --diff-base escape; pinned by a regression test. Journaled, since it is outside the kill inventory's boundary.

reason.specifics: Session 3 closes the set with the anti-resurrection grep gate, the guided-look UAT walk, and the staged major release. The gate's exemption list is the hard part and it is now shaped by BOTH prior sessions: S1's fail-loud loader and its tests must be exempt, and S2 added the historical note, the migration notice, the superseded Set 048 notice, the REMOVED blocks in two schema docs, the extension README's upgrade note, and the retirement comments in drift_guard/test.yml/uat-matrix README. An orchestrator without that context would write a gate that fails on this set's own documentation. S2 also deliberately KEPT drift_guard's iter_scanned_docs/_is_excluded doc-walk, with a comment, so S3 inherits the live-guidance vs frozen-history distinction instead of re-deriving it. Full notes in ai-assignment.md.
